# Voice research: words the voices find hard

<!-- Generated from packages/show/tools/data/voice-research.json by `npm run voice-research -- --page`. Do not edit by hand. -->

What the show's synthesized voices are heard saying, word by word, as the fitting tool's
transcription hears them. It is for a writer to scan in a minute before writing a line, and for
a sound editor to start from a spelling that has worked before.

**The owner's ruling (21 November 2026): best effort on pronunciation is sufficient, as subtitles
carry the line.** A writer may still use a hard word. Captions are on by default and follow every
line with the current word lit, so a viewer always reads the exact words. Nothing here is a reason
to cut a line, and a real person's words are never changed to suit the voice.

Voices are the house cast's ids; "guest" is any guest's voice. Spellings go in a line's `as`
field, never in its `text`.

## Unstable

Heard in some takes or some lines, not others.

| word | voices | heard as | spellings tried | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **at least** | guest, sibyl | "at least" ×8, "but it's just", "but each" | `att-leest` → "headlier teeth" ×4; `at-leest` → "to piece" ×4 | Heard in about half the takes in a guest's voice, and as written in Sibyl's ("At least" ×4); a comma after it picked up a false "won't". |
| **half** | guest | "head", "hit", "health", "heath" | `one-half` → "hit" ×8, "head" ×3; `one-haff` → "heath" ×2, "head" ×1; `wun-half` → "head" ×4; `wun-haaf` → "head, head, head (a runaway)" ×4 | Lost at the end of a line in nine spellings (head, hit, heath, the fifth); heard mid-line, in a list ("plus a-half") and in 2 of 4 takes of "half as large". |
| **mouth** | larry | "mouse" | — | Heard as "mouse"; the line was reworded before other spellings were tried. |
| **multitudes** | sibyl | "multi-toad" ×3, "molecules", "my food" | `mul-tee-toodz` → "multi-toad" ×3, "multitudes" ×1 | Heard about one take in four. |
| **plausibly** | sibyl | "plause to be" | `plaw-zib-lee` → "plausibly" ×1, "it'll probably be" ×3 | `plaw-zib-lee` heard once in four takes; otherwise "it'll probably be". |
| **sheet** | sibyl | "(a crude word)", "sheet" ×4 | — | After "other's" it was heard as a crude word, which is never accepted; respelling the word before it (`uh-therz`) cleared it. |
| **show** | larry | "flow" ×3, "fall", "phone", "foe" | `shoh` → "shah" ×4, "shot" ×2; `sshoww` → "shawl" ×1 | As written heard "flow", "fall", "phone": `showw` was heard in two lines, `sshow` in one, but `sshoww` gave "shawl" and `shoh` "shah". |
| **values** | guest | (not recorded) | `val-yooz` → "values" ×3, "value is" ×1 | `val-yooz` heard in 3 of 4 takes; the fourth, "value is", changed the sentence. |

## Patterns

Not single words.

| pattern | note |
|---|---|
| A line of one or two words | Easily lost or misheard ("Nobody." as "No bad day", a two-word line never heard); a comma between the words or a respelling helps, a longer line more. |
| A word beginning "cl" | The "cl" is voiced to "gl" ("clue" was "glue" in every take and spelling). |
| A word beginning with the "j" sound | "Judge" was never heard and "joke" was lost; a `d` before it (`djaw`) is the known try. |
| A final "th" | "Mouth" was heard as "mouse" and "math" as "mess" until spelled `mathh`. |
| A short question | One looped into a hallucinated "God is it? God is it?": a religious word is never accepted; rate 0.9 and a gap before the line stopped the loop. |
| A handle read aloud | Heard as ordinary words or a near name, never as the handle; the card and the caption carry it, and no waiver is needed. |
| A name with a possessive 's straight after another word | Never heard in six spellings; it became "which means", which changed what the line said. |
| A comma inside a real person's line | A pause can add a word: a comma after "at least" picked up a false "won't". Listen for a negation gained. |
| A clock time said in words | "Twelve thirty-eight" was heard as "12th date" in every take; the clock on screen carries it. |
